claims.claim_en: The phrase «خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) describing constancy in the Gardens.
The governor (the element to which the ḥāl relates) is the phrase «لهم» — the hal relates to 'for them'.

claims.source_quote_ar: وَإِنْ شِئْتَ كَانَ حَالًا مِنَ الضَّمِيرِ فِي «لَهُمْ» وَهُوَ أَقْوَى.
claims.claim_ar: وجهٌ آخر: يمكن اعتبارها حالًا من الضمير المستضمن في «لهم» (والكاتب يرى هذا أقوى).
claims.claim_en: Alternate analysis: the ḥāl may be taken as coming from the pronoun contained in «لهم» (the author regards this reading as stronger).
claims.needs_review_reason: The author presents this as an alternative and indicates a preference; further comparison of precedent and syntactic implications is recommended.

claims.claim_ar: فِيهَا ظرف مكان يدخل في معنى الحال «خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا» ومتعلّق بـ «لهم»/الجنّات.
claims.claim_en: فِيهَا is a locative adverbial forming part of the hal «خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا», attached to the governor «لهم» (or to 'the Gardens').

claims.source_quote_ar: (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا) : قَدْ ذُكِرَ فِي الرُّومِ.
claims.claim_ar: عبارة «وعد الله حقّا» مذكورة أيضاً في موضع سابق في سورة الروم (ملاحظة استقرائية/دراسية).
claims.claim_en: Note: the phrase «وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا» is noted as having been mentioned previously in Surah Ar-Rum (cross-reference/study note).
claims.needs_review_reason: This is a cross-reference / exegetical note rather than a syntactic parsing claim; include for study but not a formal iʿrāb rule.
